why: The quote is real and the identifier really is absent, but the stated CONSEQUENCE is demonstrably false and inverted — this is trap shape #3 from inert-worklist.md §4 ('the identifier really is unwired while the consequence is false, because something upstream already handled it'). (1) QUOTE — verbatim at whats-new/2026-w29.md:62, fetched with curl -sL. It is a one-sentence <div> in the 'Other wins' grid; nothing in the line or its neighbours (:61 vimInsertModeRemaps, :63 session-wide caps) reverses it. (2) IDENTIFIER — confirmed absent. grep -ran -F over the whole repo for 'forward-subagent-text', 'FORWARD_SUBAGENT' and 'forwardSubagent' returns hits ONLY in docs/superpowers/specs sweep artifacts; zero in packages/, apps/, scripts/, and zero even in the vendored Claude Agent SDK bundles. No flag, no env var, no camelCase reader. (3) CONSEQUENCE — FALSE, and inverted. The claim says we have 'no way to include subagent text or thinking blocks' in stream-json. In fact BOTH are included unconditionally. apps/cli/src/index.ts:469-471 is the entire stream-json path: `if (streamJson) { process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(ev) + '\n') }` — every session:event is serialised verbatim, and the only guard above it is the same-session check at :467. The parentToolUseId filtering that would exclude subagent text exists but is scoped exclusively to the NON-stream-json branches (:481 `!streamJson && !structuredMode && !sawTextDelta && !ev.parentToolUseId`, :485). The comment at :479-480 makes the intent explicit: 'Subagent (Task) child turns emit non-intermediate text_complete with parentToolUseId set'. Nothing upstream strips them either: SessionManager.sendEvent (:18449-18460) forwards every SessionEvent unconditionally, and parentToolUseId is CARRIED ONTO the emitted event (:17698, :17740), never used to suppress. Both backends populate it (claude/event-adapter.ts:398,409 from parent_tool_use_id; tool-matching.ts:189,207). THINKING likewise: there is no separate 'thinking' member of the AgentEvent union (core/src/types/message.ts:966-999) because pi/event-adapter.ts converts it into ordinary text events — :554-564 yields `text_delta` with turnId 'thinking-N' on thinking_delta, and flushThinking (:316-333) yields `text_complete` with isIntermediate:true on thinking_end (the file's own header comment at :144 states 'message_update (thinking_delta/thinking_end) -> intermediate text_delta/text_complete'). Those are session:events, so :470 dumps them too. EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED by executing sendAndStream against a stub client: with outputFormat 'stream-json' the output contained all four lines including {"type":"text_complete",...,"text":"SUBAGENT SAID THIS","parentToolUseId":"toolu_99"} and {"type":"text_complete",...,"text":"INNER THINKING","isIntermediate":true,"turnId":"thinking-1"}. POSITIVE CONTROL (required for an absence-of-filtering claim): the identical event sequence with outputFormat 'text' printed only 'plan-a' — the subagent line and the thinking completion were both suppressed. So the filtering machinery exists and demonstrably works on the same rig; it simply does not apply to stream-json. NOT an owner decision: none of the nine dated decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries) touches the CLI output surface. NOT a de-brand artifact for the flag half (the fork adopts Claude's exact spellings where it has implemented the headless contract — --output-format, --json-schema, --safe-mode), though the CLAUDE_CODE_ env prefix would never be adopted verbatim given the NESSY_ convention. The finding is refuted on its consequence: it reports a missing capability where the capability is unconditionally on.
correctedState: Refuted — the consequence is inverted. Subagent text AND thinking blocks are ALREADY in our stream-json output, always, and there is no way to turn them OFF. apps/cli/src/index.ts:469-471 serialises every session:event verbatim when --output-format stream-json is set; the parentToolUseId guard that hides subagent text lives only in the !streamJson branches (:481, :485), and thinking is carried as ordinary text_delta/text_complete events (turnId 'thinking-N', isIntermediate:true) by pi/event-adapter.ts:554-564 and :316-333, so it rides the same unconditional dump. Verified by executing sendAndStream: stream-json emitted the parentToolUseId-bearing and the thinking events; the same events in text mode printed neither (positive control). The true divergence, if one is to be filed, is the OPPOSITE of the one claimed and is a defaults/controllability difference rather than a missing feature: Claude defaults this content OFF and gates inclusion behind an opt-in --forward-subagent-text / CLAUDE_CODE_FORWARD_SUBAGENT_TEXT, whereas our CLI forwards it unconditionally with no opt-out. A consumer written against Claude's default therefore gets MORE than it expects from us (subagent chatter and raw reasoning interleaved into the parent stream, distinguishable only by the parentToolUseId field and the 'thinking-' turnId prefix), not less. Note also that both halves of the doc sentence are one feature: the flag and the env var are two spellings of the same opt-in, and neither is meaningful for a fork whose stream is already unfiltered. Row f179 already lists --forward-subagent-text among the eleven headless flags with no per-invocation equivalent, which is the accurate framing; f240 restates it with a false consequence attached and should be dropped rather than duplicated.
